title: A broken recompute returns RECOMPUTE_ERROR, not a false OK

args.code:
import Part
import Sketcher
body = doc.addObject('PartDesign::Body', 'Body')
sketch = body.newObject('Sketcher::SketchObject', 'Sketch')
sketch.AttachmentSupport = [(doc.getObject('XY_Plane') or body.Origin.OriginFeatures[3], '')]
sketch.MapMode = 'FlatFace'
points = [App.Vector(0, 0, 0), App.Vector(20, 0, 0), App.Vector(20, 20, 0), App.Vector(0, 20, 0)]
for i in range(4):
    sketch.addGeometry(Part.LineSegment(points[i], points[(i + 1) % 4]))
for i in range(4):
    sketch.addConstraint(Sketcher.Constraint('Coincident', i, 2, (i + 1) % 4, 1))
pad = body.newObject('PartDesign::Pad', 'Pad')
pad.Profile = sketch
pad.Length = 10
doc.recompute()
clean_volume = pad.Shape.Volume
sketch.deleteAllGeometry()
doc.recompute()
result = [clean_volume, pad.State, pad.getStatusString()]

agent_check: Read the capture: the FreeCAD tree marks the failing object (Pad) with an error icon, and the 3D view still shows the last valid 20 x 20 x 10 block (FreeCAD keeps it on a failed recompute). If the fit step did not return OK (the test case expects the MCP fit may refuse a faulted document), the capture is unframed: click the GUI Fit All toolbar button, capture the window and judge that. A tree with no error marker on Pad is a finding.
